title: Week-scale sparklines and sampled index layer for Console usage exploration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a compact, low-latency timeseries summary (sparkline) and a lightweight sampled row-index for tenant+route+feature-level exploratory queries in Console. Motivation: current interactive UI panels and ad-hoc debug queries hit large invocation_facts tables causing slow page loads and expensive scans. Deliver a two-tier surface: 1) micro-aggregates (per-tenant, per-route, weekly buckets, 7-day moving windows) optimized for immediate UI rendering; 2) a consistent, reproducible sampled index (hash-based sampling with TTL tiers) that supports fast drill-down queries without full scans. This ticket covers schema design, ETL plan, materialization cadence, storage/retention trade-offs, and a first-pass implementation + benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Sparkline materialized view exists with columns: tenant_id, route_id, feature, week_start, count, token_sum, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, unique_users_estimate
Sparkline query for a single tenant+route (7-day window) returns within 120ms on dev/prod-preview cluster (95th percentile).
Sampled index table exists with deterministic sampling (sha256(id) mod N <= K) documented and reproducible across replays.
A dashboard panel in Console UI consumes the sparkline API and shows 7-day sparklines for the top 10 routes for a tenant without triggering full fact scans.
ETL job runs within the window (daily refresh with incremental upsert) and has end-to-end tests + smoke queries in CI.
Cost estimate measured and accepted by FinOps: storage increase < 8% for top 100 tenants; query cost reduced >= 40% for exploratory flows.
tasks: Design schema and partitioning strategy for sparkline and sampled_index tables
Implement Spark/DBT pipeline to compute weekly micro-aggregates with incremental upserts
Implement deterministic sampling function and staged TTL tiers (7d hot, 30d warm, 365d cold)
Add materialized view refresh orchestration and backfill plan for last 90 days
Benchmark queries (latency & cost) against current invocation_facts baseline
Add access controls and telemetry: log sample selection rate and sample-skew metrics
Add Console API endpoint and wire UI panel (frontend ticket ENG-314160)
notes: Design trade-off: full denorm (wide pre-aggregates) would minimize reads but increase storage; chosen micro-aggregate + sampled index balances cost and interactivity.
Sampling method: use hash(id || tenant_id) to avoid per-tenant bias and ensure deterministic replay across reprocessing. Parameterize sample_rate (default 0.5%).
Downsampling: for sparklines prefer time-bucketed aggregates (weekly + daily 7-day rolling windows) rather than lossy sketches to preserve simple SQL semantics.
Materialization tech: prefer existing DBT + materialized views in Snowflake/BigQuery depending on customer's warehouse; for prod hosted pipeline use our curated ETL runners.
Edge cases: very high-throughput tenants will require sharded upserts or streaming compaction to avoid long-running merges; ENG-305000 owns shard-mgmt primitives.
